Scope and intent.scope.boundary: The model or block boundary, external dependencies and ownership shall be explicitly defined within the selected governed scope
Scope and intent.scope.purpose: The model or block purpose shall be sufficiently defined for both RTL and high-level model generation
Scope and intent.scope.behavior: Included behavior, exclusions and assumptions shall be explicit; outside-scope behavior shall remain visible without being inferred or implemented

Interfaces.io.names: Every admitted in-scope signal or port shall have an explicit, traceable name
Interfaces.io.direction: Every admitted in-scope signal or port direction shall be defined relative to its owning block
Interfaces.io.width: Every admitted in-scope signal or port width shall be defined, including applicable parameterization and legal values
Interfaces.io.grouping: Interface membership, signal grouping and local signal-to-standard mapping shall be explicit where relevant
Interfaces.io.standard: For each interface, governed evidence shall identify either a recognized standard with an unambiguous applicable specification or full custom behavior. AMBA, AHB, APB, AXI, I2C, SPI, LIN and UART are examples, not an exhaustive list. A family name, acronym or vague reference alone shall not establish standard coverage. Verify the role, subset or mode, deviations, sidebands and integration constraints under the following items; valid standard coverage shall replace, not duplicate, checks of standard-defined signal semantics, interpretation, handshakes and timing. Non-standard, partially identified or undocumented deviating behavior shall receive full custom-interface checks
Interfaces.io.role: The block role and endpoints on each interface shall be defined, including the applicable initiator, target, controller, peripheral, transmitter or receiver role
Interfaces.io.mode: Each standard interface's supported subset, mode and applicable version or revision shall be unambiguous where relevant; unsupported features shall not be inferred
Interfaces.io.meaning: Every in-scope signal meaning shall be defined locally or validly covered by io.standard; standard-defined semantics shall not require redundant restatement
Interfaces.io.interpretation: Signal value interpretation, encodings and valid values shall be defined locally or validly covered by io.standard; local extensions shall be checked explicitly
Interfaces.io.handshake: Required transfer, handshake, flow-control and backpressure behavior shall be defined locally or validly covered by io.standard without redundant revalidation of standard-defined behavior
Interfaces.io.deviations: Local deviations from a standard shall be explicitly defined and checked, or governed evidence shall establish that none apply; undocumented deviations shall force custom checks for affected behavior
Interfaces.io.sideband: Local sideband and extra signals shall be explicitly identified and checked independently of standard coverage, or governed evidence shall establish their non-applicability
Interfaces.io.integration: Local integration constraints not covered by the standard shall be defined, including relevant clock, reset, timing, electrical or operating assumptions; standard coverage shall be bounded to the exact interfaces and behavior it supports

Clocks and resets.clock.identity: All behaviorally relevant clocks, sources and operating conditions shall be identified
Clocks and resets.clock.synchrony: Synchronous relationships and asynchronous signals or interfaces shall be explicitly identified where relevant
Clocks and resets.reset.identity: All behaviorally relevant resets and their sources shall be identified
Clocks and resets.reset.polarity: Each reset's active polarity shall be explicit
Clocks and resets.reset.semantics: Each reset's synchronous or asynchronous type, assertion and release semantics shall be explicit
Clocks and resets.reset.initialization: Initial state, reset values, post-reset behavior and conditions for resuming operation shall be defined where needed
Clocks and resets.clock.domains: The clock and reset domain of each signal or interface shall be defined where relevant, including domain relationships
Clocks and resets.clock.cdc: Applicable clock-domain and reset-domain crossing boundaries and synchronization expectations shall be explicit; synchronizers or crossing behavior shall not be guessed
Clocks and resets.clock.power: Clock gating, power gating, isolation, retention and entry or exit sequencing shall be defined only when behaviorally relevant to the governed scope

FSMs and control behavior.control.identity: Required state machines or control domains shall be identified without inventing an FSM decomposition
FSMs and control behavior.control.states: States, control roles and observable behavior shall be sufficiently defined
FSMs and control behavior.control.transitions: Transition conditions, priorities, guards and relevant outputs shall be sufficiently defined
FSMs and control behavior.control.initialization: Initial and reset control states and startup behavior shall be explicit
FSMs and control behavior.control.interactions: Interactions and ordering between state machines and control domains shall be defined where relevant
FSMs and control behavior.control.recovery: Applicable illegal-state, safe-state, fault and recovery behavior shall be defined without assuming an implementation

Functional behavior.function.main: All implementation-critical in-scope functions and observable results shall be sufficiently defined
Functional behavior.function.triggers: Triggering, enabling and completion conditions shall be defined
Functional behavior.function.sequence: Required functional sequencing, concurrency and ordering constraints shall be defined
Functional behavior.function.priority: Priority, arbitration and simultaneous-event behavior shall be defined where needed
Functional behavior.function.errors: Error, exception, cancellation and recovery behavior shall be defined where relevant

Datapath and data semantics.data.transformations: Required data transformations, input-output relationships and applicable algorithms shall be defined
Datapath and data semantics.data.arithmetic: Arithmetic operations, units, ranges and data interpretation shall be explicit where relevant
Datapath and data semantics.data.format: Data formats, encodings, byte ordering and fixed-point or floating-point representations shall be defined where relevant
Datapath and data semantics.data.signedness: Signed or unsigned interpretation and conversions shall be explicit where relevant
Datapath and data semantics.data.precision: Required precision, scaling, rounding, truncation and saturation behavior shall be explicit where relevant
Datapath and data semantics.data.overflow: Overflow and underflow behavior, including reporting or recovery, shall be defined where relevant
Datapath and data semantics.data.latency: Data-path latency, buffering, ordering and validity relationships shall be defined where relevant

Configuration, CSR, memory and registers.config.effects: Configuration fields and their functional effects, update visibility and side effects shall be defined where relevant
Configuration, CSR, memory and registers.config.illegal: Illegal, reserved and unsupported configurations and required responses shall be explicit where applicable
Configuration, CSR, memory and registers.config.dependencies: Configuration dependencies, access ordering and sequencing constraints shall be defined where relevant
Configuration, CSR, memory and registers.config.csr: Applicable CSR and register maps shall define addresses, bitfields, permissions, reset values, reserved bits and field effects; register-map evidence shall not be treated as interface or I/O evidence
Configuration, CSR, memory and registers.config.memory: Applicable memory access behavior, organization, capacity, widths, ports, arbitration and initialization shall be defined, including relevant FIFO, RAM, ROM and buffering characteristics
Configuration, CSR, memory and registers.config.buffering: Applicable buffer or FIFO ordering, full or empty behavior, overflow or underflow handling and backpressure shall be explicit

Timing, ordering and performance constra.timing.sequence: Required timing relationships, sequencing, ordering and completion conditions shall be sufficiently defined
Timing, ordering and performance constra.timing.local: Custom timing, non-standard handshakes, deviations and integration-specific constraints shall be explicit; behavior already validly covered by io.standard shall not be redundantly revalidated
Timing, ordering and performance constra.timing.standard: Applicable standard references shall establish the required standard-defined timing and handshake behavior under io.standard; local exceptions shall remain explicit checks rather than demanding restatement of the standard
Timing, ordering and performance constra.timing.performance: Required latency, throughput, service rate, deadlines and relevant operating conditions shall be defined where applicable

Internal structure and composition.structure.parts: Necessary parts, internal domains and composition boundaries shall be sufficiently represented using governed evidence only
Internal structure and composition.structure.interactions: Implementation-critical dependencies, interactions and composition contracts shall be defined; block relations shall not imply physical wiring
Internal structure and composition.structure.support: No unsupported inferred structure or connection shall be present; containment, block relations and directed signal connections shall retain their distinct evidence requirements

Consistency and conflict checks.consistency.contradictions: No unresolved material conflict shall remain across requirements, descriptions, tables, diagrams, models and applicable standard references
Consistency and conflict checks.consistency.ambiguity: No unresolved ambiguity shall permit materially different implementation-critical behavior

Traceability and governed evidence suppo.consistency.traceability: Functions, interfaces, data, configuration, timing and control shall be traceable to admitted governed inputs within approved scope; candidate or unadmitted evidence shall not establish support
Traceability and governed evidence suppo.consistency.snapshot: The selected immutable snapshot, allocations, ownership, scope and downstream coherence shall be valid and consistently bound across all assessment inputs
Traceability and governed evidence suppo.evidence.authority: Readiness shall not outrun governed authority, invent missing facts, infer intent or create an approval lane; applicable standards shall have traceable governed applicability and reference support

Residual gaps and readiness blockers.residual.classification: Unresolved, ambiguous, conflicting, intentionally omitted, outside-scope and source-update-needed gaps shall remain visible and classified with provenance, disposition and readiness impact; parser gaps shall not be misrepresented as source absence
Residual gaps and readiness blockers.residual.material: No unresolved implementation-critical gap shall prevent trustworthy RTL or high-level model generation; generation with gaps shall not imply READY, and omissions or future source updates shall not waive required information

Optional DFT, DFX and diagnostics.diagnostics.behavior: DFT, DFX, test access, observability, fault reporting and diagnostic behavior shall be checked when explicitly required by applicable governed policy. This section is informational by default, not a universal readiness blocker; explicit policy requirements shall make it blocking and require governed evidence

Final READY or NOT READY decision.readiness.decision: The central assessor shall declare READY only when every required applicable obligation is sufficiently defined or validly covered by standard references, non-applicability is evidenced, and snapshot, coherence, traceability, dependency and critical residual-gap gates pass. Otherwise it shall declare NOT READY, fail closed and preserve visible reasons; generation or publication success shall not substitute for implementation readiness
